recorded: Hand-authored. No live model produced this run; it is the record of what /iterate-visual must do when three passes are not enough. Every verdict below describes the image the pinned house style actually produces for the spec it names, and src/revise.test.ts renders those specs and holds the verdicts to them.

items.note: The spec turns the value axis grid back on: horizontal gridlines behind twelve bars, and a tick label every two points, none of which a value is read off.
One comparison, repeated across six weeks: checklist against control.
The title reads 'Retention by signup week and arm', which names the axes rather than the Claim.
No share is written beside any bar, and the house style draws no legend, so every value has to be traced across to the axis and neither arm is named on the image.
The house style's categorical range is the accent then grey, so the checklist bars come out accent and the control bars grey; nothing else on the image carries colour.
Accent and grey differ in lightness as well as hue; the pairs stay distinct rendered without colour.
The value axis runs 20% to 45%, so a three-point gap looks like a doubling.

passes.revision: Turn the gridlines off, rewrite charts[].title to the Claim sentence, and pin the colour scale in the spec so the checklist arm keeps the accent instead of depending on the order the categories arrive in.

items.note: The gridlines are gone; what is left is twelve bars, six week labels and a value axis.
Unchanged: one comparison across six weeks.
The title is now the Claim sentence with the two shares in it.
Still nothing written beside a bar: colour separates the two arms, but no value is on the image and neither arm is named.
Unchanged, and now pinned by the spec's own colour scale rather than left to the order the categories arrive in.
Unchanged from pass 1: accent and grey differ in lightness, not only in hue.
The value axis still runs 20% to 45%.

passes.revision: Set the value scale domain to 0–0.5 and add a layered text mark writing each share above its bar.

items.note: No gridlines, no border, and the house style draws no legend; every mark on the image carries a value.
Unchanged: one comparison across six weeks.
Unchanged from pass 2: the title is the Claim sentence.
Each of the twelve bars now carries its share, but nothing on the image names the arms: with no legend drawn, which of each pair is the checklist has to be said in prose.
Unchanged from pass 2: checklist accent, control grey, nothing else coloured.
Unchanged from pass 2: accent and grey differ in lightness.
The value axis now runs 0 to 50%, so bar length is proportional to the share.

outcome.next_step: Every bar carries its share, but neither arm is ever named on the image, and the validated Vega-Lite subset bans transform, datum and condition, so a series label can be written on all twelve bars or on none — twenty-four labels at this width. Two ways out, and the choice is the Operator's: show the six weeks as two labelled lines, where two labels name both arms; or keep the bars, name the arms in the Claim's prose and carry the weekly numbers in its table. Three passes is a maximum, so this chart is not recorded as passing; whether it stays on the Reader's page until one of those is chosen is the Operator's call, and holding it back means dropping its id from the Claim's chart_ids and its marker from the memo.
outcome.note: Six of seven items pass. The score is not the acceptance test: one failing item returns the chart.

variants.why_rejected: Gridlines and a truncated axis; kept so the Operator can see what was tried.
Decluttered but still starts the value axis at 20%.
